events.title: First assembler program runs
events.summary: On May 6, 1949, David Wheeler's program on the EDSAC computer translated short text labels into machine instructions — the first assembler.
events.about: Before this, programmers had to punch raw binary numbers for every instruction. Wheeler's program let them write short labels like `A 80` instead of 17-bit binary patterns. Every compiler and operating system since then builds on this idea: humans write readable code, a program translates it for the machine.

narrative.whyChosen: Before assemblers, programmers punched binary instruction words by hand — one wrong bit broke the whole run.
narrative.whyImportant: Automating mnemonic-to-machine-code translation made programming repeatable and launched the software industry.
narrative.problemSolved: Human transcription of machine instructions was slow, error-prone, and did not scale as computers grew more capable.
